questions.stem: Who was the historical founder of the Haryanka dynasty, often considered the first major historically documented ruling dynasty of the powerful Magadha empire?
questions.explanation: Bimbisara (c. 544 – 492 BCE) was the founder of the Haryanka dynasty. He expanded Magadha's power through conquests (like Anga) and strategic matrimonial alliances. Chandragupta and Ashoka belonged to the later Maurya dynasty.

questions.stem: Which Magadhan ruler from the Haryanka dynasty famously transferred the capital of the empire from Rajagriha to the newly built city of Pataliputra?
questions.explanation: Udayin (or Udayabhadra), the son of Ajatashatru, shifted the capital from Rajagriha to Pataliputra (modern-day Patna) because of its highly strategic location at the confluence of the Ganga and Son rivers.

questions.stem: Bimbisara, the powerful King of Magadha from the Haryanka dynasty, was a known contemporary of which great religious figure?
questions.explanation: Bimbisara was a close contemporary of both Gautama Buddha and Mahavira. Buddhist texts state he was a patron of Buddha, while Jain texts claim he was a follower of Mahavira.

questions.explanation: Wait, let's look at the clean explanation: Ajatashatru engaged in a long 16-year war against the powerful Vajjian Confederacy, led by the Licchavis of Vaishali. He finally defeated them by sowing discord among their leaders.

questions.stem: Who was the highly ambitious and powerful founder of the Nanda dynasty, famously referred to in Puranic texts as 'Ekarat' (the sole sovereign)?
questions.explanation: Mahapadma Nanda usurped the throne from the Shishunagas. He is often called the first great historical emperor of Northern India. He conquered several Kshatriya states and assumed the title 'Ekarat'.

questions.stem: The Nanda dynasty was the dominant ruling power strictly situated in Magadha during the famous military invasion of North-West India by which foreign conqueror?
questions.explanation: When Alexander the Great invaded North-West India (around 326 BCE), Dhana Nanda, the last ruler of the Nanda dynasty, was ruling Magadha. The massive size of the Nanda army was a major reason Alexander's troops mutinied and refused to march further east.
